title.en: Find the transpose and use its properties
Write a square matrix as a sum of the two

say.en: Turn a table so that its rows become columns. Some matrices look exactly the same after this flip; others become their own negative. In this lesson: Find the transpose and use its properties.
Identify symmetric and skew-symmetric matrices.
Write a square matrix as a sum of the two.

body.en: The *transpose* $A'$ (or $A^T$) is obtained by interchanging rows and columns: if $A = [a_{ij}]_{m \times n}$ then $A' = [a_{ji}]_{n \times m}$. Properties: $(A')' = A$, $(kA)' = kA'$, $(A + B)' = A' + B'$, and $(AB)' = B'A'$.
body.kn: ಸಾಲು ಮತ್ತು ಕಂಬಸಾಲುಗಳನ್ನು ಅದಲು ಬದಲು ಮಾಡಿದರೆ ಪರಿವರ್ತ A′ ಸಿಗುತ್ತದೆ. (A′)′ = A, (A + B)′ = A′ + B′, (AB)′ = B′A′.

narration.en: The transpose swaps rows and columns. Transposing twice gives back A, and the transpose of a product is the product of transposes in reverse order.
narration.kn: ಸಾಲು ಮತ್ತು ಕಂಬಸಾಲುಗಳನ್ನು ಅದಲು ಬದಲು ಮಾಡಿದರೆ ಪರಿವರ್ತ A′ ಸಿಗುತ್ತದೆ. (A′)′ = A, (A + B)′ = A′ + B′, (AB)′ = B′A′.

say.en: The transpose swaps rows and columns. Transposing twice gives back A, and the transpose of a product is the product of transposes in reverse order.
say.kn: ಸಾಲು ಮತ್ತು ಕಂಬಸಾಲುಗಳನ್ನು ಅದಲು ಬದಲು ಮಾಡಿದರೆ ಪರಿವರ್ತ A′ ಸಿಗುತ್ತದೆ. (A′)′ = A, A plus B′ = A′ plus B′, AB′ = B′A′.

say.en: A plus B' = A' plus B'.
AB' = B'A' order reverses.
The transpose turns rows into columns. A 2 by 3 matrix becomes a 3 by 2 matrix.
Symmetric means A transpose equals A: the matrix is a mirror image in its diagonal. Skew-symmetric means A transpose is minus A, so the diagonal is all zeros.
Every square matrix splits into a symmetric part plus a skew-symmetric part.
One more rule: the transpose of a product reverses the order.

body.en: A square matrix is *symmetric* if $A' = A$ ($a_{ij} = a_{ji}$) and skew-symmetric if $A' = -A$ ($a_{ij} = -a_{ji}$, so every diagonal element is 0). Every square matrix is uniquely $A = \frac{1}{2}(A + A') + \frac{1}{2}(A - A')$: symmetric part plus skew-symmetric part.
body.kn: A′ = A ಆದರೆ ಸಮಮಿತೀಯ, A′ = −A ಆದರೆ ವಿಷಮಮಿತೀಯ (ಕರ್ಣ ಅಂಶಗಳು ಶೂನ್ಯ). ಪ್ರತಿ ಚೌಕ ಮಾತೃಕೆ = ಸಮಮಿತೀಯ ಭಾಗ + ವಿಷಮಮಿತೀಯ ಭಾಗ.

points.en: A + A' is *symmetric*; A − A' is skew-symmetric

narration.en: A symmetric matrix equals its transpose; a skew-symmetric matrix equals minus its transpose, so its diagonal is all zero. Any square matrix splits into a symmetric part plus a skew-symmetric part.

say.en: Skew-symmetric: A' = -A, diagonal all zero.
A plus A' is symmetric; A - A' is skew-symmetric.

caption.en: A = [a b; c d]. P = ½(A + A′) is symmetric, Q = ½(A − A′) is skew-symmetric, and P + Q = A.

Make c = −b. What is left of the symmetric part off the diagonal?

narration.en: Move the entries. The off-diagonal of the symmetric part is the average of b and c; the skew part takes half their difference.

problem.en: Express A = [3 5; 1 −1] as the sum of a symmetric and a skew-symmetric matrix.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Express A = [3 5; 1 −1] as the sum of a symmetric and a skew-symmetric matrix.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Express A = [3 5; 1 minus 1] as the sum of a symmetric and a skew-symmetric matrix.
P equals one half (A plus A') equals one half [6 6; 6 minus 2] = [3 3; 3 minus 1] symmetric.
Q equals one half (A - A') equals one half [0 4; minus 4 0] = [0 2; minus 2 0] (skew-symmetric).
So the answer is A = [3 3; 3 minus 1] plus [0 2; minus 2 0].

body.en: Look at the diagonal first: any non-zero entry there rules out skew-symmetry. Then check mirror pairs across the diagonal: symmetric pairs are equal, skew pairs are negatives.
